title: Payment domain model
idea: The payment domain model separates what is paid (Money), how it is paid (PaymentMethod), and what happened to it (Payment, Refund, PaymentStatus).

analogy.text: A shop receipt book. Each receipt records the amount, how the customer paid, and any money handed back, written under the original line.
analogy.breaks: Paper never refuses a refund larger than the sale.

points: Money is a value object: a long in minor units plus a currency.
PaymentMethod is an interface; UPIPayment and CardPayment implement it.
A Payment has one method, one amount, and zero or more Refunds.
Payment guards its invariant: refunds never add up past the amount.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: A Payment holds its amount as Money. The running refunded total is Money too.

edges.label: paid by 1
edges.caption: Each Payment is made with exactly one PaymentMethod.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: UPIPayment is-a PaymentMethod. It holds a UPI id and checks its format.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: CardPayment is-a PaymentMethod. It keeps a gateway token and the last four digits, never the card number.

edges.label: has 0..*
edges.caption: A Payment owns its Refunds. Each Refund points back by paymentId.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: A Refund amount is Money in the same currency as its payment.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: PaymentStatus is an enum. The lifecycle page turns it into a state machine.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for values, a class for Payment because its status and totals change. Invariants live in constructors and methods.

walk.text: Build a UPI payment of 49900 paise for order ORD-7 with key k-1.
Mark it succeeded, then refund 20000 and 29900: partial, then full.
Four bad inputs; each is refused with a message.
Money rejects negative amounts and bad currency codes, and adds without rounding.
Each method validates its own fields. The card record never holds a card number.
The constructor rejects a zero amount and starts the refunded total at zero.
refund checks status and remaining balance, then updates both together.

pitfalls: Never store a full card number; keep a gateway token and the last four digits.
Use long minor units for money; double cannot hold 0.1 exactly.
Keep refunds as their own records, not a single refunded flag.

quiz.q: What does PaymentModel print for the refund R-3 of 1?
quiz.why: After R-2 the refunded total equals the amount, so status is REFUNDED. The status check runs before the balance check.

takeaway: Money, method and history are separate types; Payment guards the totals.

starters: Why is Money a record instead of a plain long?
Should PaymentMethod be a sealed interface in Java 17?
How would I add a wallet as a third payment method?
